claim_pc.text: Directed bond percolation is critical at bond density p_c = 0.644700185(5).

claim.source: Hinrichsen, Adv. Phys. 49, 815 (2000); Jensen, J. Phys. A 32, 5233 (1999)
claim.text: Directed-percolation density decay exponent delta = 0.159464(6) in 1+1 dimensions.

verdict.text: within the stated tolerance of +/-0.05; the bootstrap interval still contains the quoted value, so this is a statement about precision as much as about the value

noise.note: dyadic m/2^k, so each value is exact and no probability is rounded

claim.source: Toom (1974); Gacs, J. Stat. Phys. 103, 307 (2001); Toom, arXiv:2306.13226
claim.text: Toom's theorem: below a nonzero noise threshold, NEC majority stores a bit for a time that diverges with the lattice; symmetric majority does not.

toom.loss: the bit is lost when fewer than half the cells still hold the initial value; a run that reaches the cap is a lower bound, drawn as >= cap

tower.note: A pedagogical analogue, not Gacs's construction: leaf errors are independent, the tree is shallow, and no threshold is claimed for it. Gacs's 1D construction has to defeat correlated errors inside a cellular neighbourhood, which is why it is far more intricate.
